facts.statement: Harrison originally described Paracathartes as the earliest known vulture of the Cathartidae family.
facts.quote: Paracathartes was described by Harrison as the earliest known cathartid vulture.

facts.statement: Rich criticized Harrison's assignment of Paracathartes to the vulture family.
Houde classified Paracathartes as a member of the order Lithornithiformes and family Lithornithidae in 1988.
facts.quote: Houde (1988) included it as a member of the order Lithornithiformes and family Lithornithidae.

facts.statement: Paracathartes was a paleognathous bird with a turkey-like stature and size, closely resembling a tinamou.
facts.quote: It is a paleognathous bird, turkey-like in stature and size, that probably resembled a tinamou quite closely.

facts.statement: Unlike other lithornithids, Paracathartes was likely a poor flyer, similar to its modern relatives.
facts.quote: Unlike other lithornithids but much like its modern relatives it was probably a poor flyer.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Paracathartes is cataloged as ROM 22658 in the Royal Ontario Museum.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is in the collection of the Royal Ontario Museum. It has catalog number ROM 22658.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of the distal end of a left tibiotarsus.
facts.quote: It is the distal end of a left tibiotarsus.

facts.statement: The holotype was collected by G. E. Lindblad and G. Sternberg on August 4, 1949.
facts.quote: It was collected by G. E. Lindblad and G. Sternberg on 4 August 1949.

facts.statement: Paracathartes fossils were found at the northernmost branch of Elk Creek near Basin, Wyoming.
facts.quote: It was found at the northernmost branch of Elk Creek, near Basin, Wyoming.

facts.statement: Paracathartes lived during the Greybullian, middle Wasatchian (early Eocene) in the Willwood Formation of the Bighorn Basin.
facts.quote: The horizon is Greybullian, middle Wasatchian (early Eocene), Willwood Formation, Bighorn Basin.

facts.statement: Further collections include nearly complete skeletons from at least five individuals preserved together.
facts.quote: Further specimens of Paracathartes were collected, including almost the whole skeleton (USNM 361402-361446, 391984, 404747-404806) from at least five individuals preserved together.

facts.statement: Fossils associated with Paracathartes include three whole eggs and an avian neurocranium that may belong to the species or a phorusrhacid.
facts.quote: These bones were associated with three whole eggs (USNM 336564) and an avian neurocranium (USNM 361415) which may belong to Paracathartes or to a possible phorusrhacid.

facts.statement: Paracathartes lived between 56 and 48.07 million years ago during the Ypresian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Paracathartes is the family Lithornithidae.

rejected.statement: Paracathartes is classified within the class Aves.
